subsystems.name: Swarm robots
subsystems.role: small mobile units that deposit material layer by layer

subsystems.name: Coordination and communication
subsystems.role: lets thousands of robots work together without a central controller

subsystems.name: Material supply
subsystems.role: delivers concrete or other build material to the robots

subsystems.name: Positioning and sensing
subsystems.role: keeps each robot in the right place and aware of its neighbours

subsystems.name: Power and maintenance
subsystems.role: keeps the swarm running for long builds

subsystems.name: Build planning software
subsystems.role: turns a design into a swarm build sequence

buildSteps.title: Design for swarming
buildSteps.detail: The structure is divided into small, overlapping tasks that many robots can attempt in parallel, such as filling a wall section or laying a beam.

buildSteps.title: Set up the site
buildSteps.detail: A base station is placed on site with material storage, power and a localisation reference.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Robots are positioned and their localisation is calibrated against the base station and surveyed markers.

buildSteps.title: Start the build
buildSteps.detail: Robots move to their assigned areas and begin depositing material, following the shared plan but adjusting to neighbours.

buildSteps.title: Coordinate continuously
buildSteps.detail: Each robot broadcasts its status; algorithms reassign tasks as robots finish, fail or need refilling.

buildSteps.title: Layer by layer
buildSteps.detail: The swarm adds successive layers, with material setting fast enough to support the next pass.

buildSteps.title: Refill and recharge
buildSteps.detail: Robots automatically return to the base station for material and power, then rejoin the swarm.

buildSteps.title: Finish and cure
buildSteps.detail: Once the structure is complete, robots withdraw and the material is left to cure or is finished by other machines.

prerequisites.why: algorithms exist in lab demos but not for thousands of robots on a construction site.
single mobile robots can print concrete; coordinating many to print one structure is still research.
centimetre accuracy is needed for structural printing, and GPS is not enough indoors or between floors.
concrete mixes for gantry 3D printing are already commercial, though they must be adapted for robot swarms.
batteries and automated material refilling must work reliably for days of continuous building.
mesh networking works, but scaling to thousands of nodes with low latency is untested on sites.

pathway.milestone: lab demos of a few robots printing small structures or assembling blocks
pathway.unlocks: proof that decentralised construction is possible.

pathway.milestone: pilot projects with dozens of robots printing simple walls or shelters
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on reliability, speed and material handling.

pathway.milestone: commercial systems for rapid deployment of small buildings in remote or disaster areas
pathway.unlocks: a market and supply chain for swarm construction.

pathway.milestone: thousands-strong swarms building multi-storey structures in cities
pathway.unlocks: construction that is faster, cheaper and uses less labour.
